---
name: <short-kebab-case-slug>
description: <one-line summary, used to decide relevance during recall>
metadata:
  type: user | feedback | project | reference
---

<the fact; for feedback/project, follow with **Why:** and **How to apply:** lines. Link related memories with [[their-name]].>
```

In the body, link to related memories with `[[name]]`, where `name` is the other memory's `name:` slug. Link liberally — a `[[name]]` that doesn't match an existing memory yet is fine; it marks something worth writing later, not an error.

`user`: who the user is (role, expertise, preferences). `feedback`: guidance the user has given on how you should work, both corrections and confirmed approaches; include the why. `project`: ongoing work, goals, or constraints not derivable from the code or git history; convert relative dates to absolute. `reference`: pointers to external resources (URLs, dashboards, tickets).

After writing the file, add a one-line pointer in `MEMORY.md` (`- [Title](file.md) — hook`). `MEMORY.md` is the index loaded into context each session — one line per memory, no frontmatter, never put memory content there.

Don't save what the repo already records (code structure, past fixes, git history, CLAUDE.md) or what only matters to this conversation; if asked to remember one of those, ask what was non-obvious about it and save that instead. tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

**Do not spawn agents unless the user asks.** Each spawn starts cold and re-derives context you already have — it's the expensive path on this plan. A task with "multiple angles," "thorough," or several parts is not a request to spawn; handle it inline with your own tools. Only use this tool when the user explicitly says to use a subagent, or names one of the available agent types.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

A fork runs in the background and keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate. Subagents run in the background; you'll be notified when one completes. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).

- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- GitHub notifies the owner of any `@name` written in a PR, issue, or comment. Write a bare `@name` only for a real login you mean to notify. Put roles, placeholders, and code (`@human`, `@reviewer`, `@types/node`) in backticks or drop the `@`, even when copied from project files.
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.
- Always run `/verify` right before the `commit` command (never for docs or tests).

timeout.description: Optional timeout in milliseconds (max 600000 for a foreground command)

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

run_in_background.description: Set to true to run this command in the background.

dangerouslyDisableSandbox.description: Set this to true to dangerously override sandbox mode and run commands without sandboxing.

tools.name: Edit
tools.description:
Performs exact string replacement in a file.

- You must Read the file in this conversation before editing, or the call will fail.
- `old_string` must match the file exactly, including indentation, and be unique — the edit fails otherwise. Strip the Read line prefix (line number + tab) before matching.
- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to modify

new_string.description: The text to replace it with (must be different from old_string)

replace_all.description: Replace all occurrences of old_string (default false)

tools.name: ListAgents
tools.description: Lists agents you can SendMessage to — in-process subagents you spawned, the teammates on your team, other local Claude sessions on this machine, your Claude sessions running in the cloud (when this session has cloud access; a cloud session receives your message but cannot message any session back yet — do not ask it to reply, read its answer in its own transcript), and (when Remote Control is connected here) your account's other sessions — Remote Control sessions on other machines and cloud sessions, each row labeled by kind. Names are the address: send with `SendMessage({to: "<name>", message: "..."})`, copying the name exactly as a row prints it. Append a row's ` [ref]` only when the bare name is not enough — two rows share it, or an error asks you to disambiguate.

channel.description: Not available in this build; leave unset.

q.description: Not available in this build; leave unset.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to read

offset.description: The line number to start reading from. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once

limit.description: The number of lines to read. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once.

pages.description: Page range for PDF files (e.g., "1-5", "3", "10-20"). Only applicable to PDF files. Maximum 20 pages per request.

allow_large.description: Set to true to read a text file, or a line range of one, that is over the usual size limits, up to what still fits in your context. Only use this when you genuinely need all of it or the user asked for the whole file; otherwise read it in parts with offset and limit, or search it.

tools.name: ReportFindings
tools.description: Report code-review findings as a typed list so the host UI can render them. Use this only when the active code-review instructions tell you to report findings with this tool; otherwise follow whatever output format those instructions specify. When reporting a review's results, call it once with the verified findings ranked most-severe first (empty array if nothing survived verification) and do not also print the findings as text. When re-reporting after applying fixes (only if the apply instructions ask for it), set `outcome` on each finding to what actually happened.

level.description: Effort level the review ran at

findings.description: Verified findings, most-severe first; empty if none survived

file.description: Repo-relative path of the file the finding is in

short_summary.description: Compressed label for compact UI (≤60 chars): the claim alone, no rationale or consequence clause

category.description: Short kebab-case slug of the finding type, e.g. "correctness", "simplification", "efficiency", "test-coverage"

verdict.description: Set when a verify pass ran; absent on inline-only reviews

outcome.description: Set ONLY when re-reporting after applying fixes: what happened to this finding

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

delaySeconds.description: Seconds from now to wake up. Clamped to [60, 3600] by the runtime. Required unless `stop` is true.

reason.description: One short sentence explaining the chosen delay. Goes to telemetry and is shown to the user. Be specific. Required unless `stop` is true.

prompt.description: The /loop input to fire on wake-up. Pass the same /loop input verbatim each turn so the next firing re-enters the skill and continues the loop. For autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` instead (the dynamic-pacing variant, not the CronCreate-mode `<<autonomous-loop>>`). Required unless `stop` is true.

stop.description: Set to true to end the dynamic loop immediately instead of scheduling another wakeup. When true, all other fields are ignored and no further wakeups fire.

noop.description: true = nothing changed (you checked and there is nothing to report). false = something happened worth keeping (edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, surfaced a finding). Consecutive noop:true ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak. Required unless `stop` is true.

tools.name: SendFeedback
tools.description:
Use this tool to draft feedback about Claude Code when you hit a high-signal moment. That includes both PRODUCT issues and MODEL-BEHAVIOR issues:
- a reproducible tool or product failure was just resolved or abandoned
- the user clearly expressed frustration with Claude Code or with how you handled the task
- you hit a missing capability that blocked a reasonable request
- you notice, or the user points out, that your own behavior in this session went wrong, for example: you gave a confident answer then had to retract it; you stopped short and handed work back when you could have finished; you declined or disputed a reasonable request; you spawned more subagents than the task warranted; your tone was off; you asked more clarifying questions than needed; you expanded scope beyond what was asked

The draft is QUEUED LOCALLY. It is never sent without the user's explicit approval, and calling this tool renders no UI and does not interrupt the conversation, so never announce it or ask the user about it mid-task.

Write `details` as short labeled bullets in this exact order, one to three lines each, no narrative paragraphs:
- **What happened:** the observed behavior vs. what was expected, with exact error text if short. Facts only.
- **What the user said:** the user's own words that prompted this, quoted. If nothing did, write "User didn't comment; observed by the model." Never paraphrase sentiment into a stronger claim.
- **Repro:** the minimal steps or shape that reproduces it.
- **Evidence:** identifiers a reader can chase, such as request IDs, timestamps, file paths, versions. Omit the bullet if there are none.

Constraints:
- Never fabricate or exaggerate user sentiment; report only what actually happened.
- Everything in the draft must be sourced from the user or the session, never inferred: leave unknown fields blank rather than guess, and add a final **Cause:** bullet only for a root cause you verified in-session.
- Use `area` to name the part of Claude Code the feedback is about (a feature, command, or workflow, e.g. "hooks config", "/help", "file editing") when there is a clear one; leave it blank otherwise.
- Use `failure_mode` ONLY when the report is about model behavior (how Claude responded), not a product bug. Pick the single closest value, or `other` when it is a model-behavior issue that fits no listed value; omit the field only when the report is a product/tool bug with no model-behavior component.
- Use `task_category` to name what kind of task the session was doing, or `other` when it is a clear task that fits no listed value. Omit only if genuinely unclear.
- Do not include secrets or credentials. Refer to people by role ("a teammate", "the PR reviewer"), never by name, email address, or chat/user ID. This applies inside quoted user words too: replace a name or handle with a bracketed role (e.g. "[a teammate]") and keep the rest verbatim. Do not include customer-facing channel or DM IDs, or excerpts of customer content. Session, request, and run IDs, timestamps, repo/PR numbers, and file paths (written relative to the working directory, or ~-prefixed, not absolute paths under the user's home) remain the right evidence.
- If the issue looks like a security vulnerability: describe the class of problem, never a working exploit or step-by-step extraction path.
- Draft only at the natural moments listed above, and at most one draft per distinct issue; never re-draft the same issue in a session.

type.description: What kind of feedback this is.

title.description: Short, specific one-line summary of the issue.

details.description: Labeled bullets, in order: **What happened:** (observed vs. expected, exact error text if short); **What the user said:** (quoted, or "User didn't comment; observed by the model."); **Repro:** (minimal steps); **Evidence:** (request IDs, timestamps, paths, versions; omit if none); optionally a final **Cause:** only if verified in-session. One to three lines per bullet. No narrative paragraphs, no speculation, no secrets.

area.description: Optional short tag naming the part of Claude Code this is about (e.g. "hooks config", "/help", "file editing"). Leave blank if unclear.

failure_mode.description: When the report is about MODEL BEHAVIOR (not a product bug), the closest failure mode, or `other` when it is a model-behavior issue that fits no listed value. Omit only when the report is a product/tool bug with no model-behavior component.

task_category.description: What kind of task the session was doing when the issue occurred, or `other` when it is a clear task that fits no listed value. Omit only if genuinely unclear.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

skill.description: The name of a skill from the available-skills list. Do not guess names.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

query.description: Query to find deferred tools. Use "select:<tool_name>" for direct selection, or keywords to search.

max_results.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 5)

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

A workflow size guideline is configured for this session: small — keep workflows under 5 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale.

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with the same `scriptPath` instead of re-sending the full script. Takes precedence over `script` and `name`.

resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. Completed agent() calls with unchanged (prompt, opts) return their cached results instantly; only edited or new calls re-run. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

tools.name: Write
tools.description:
Writes a file to the local filesystem, overwriting if one exists.

When to use: creating a new file, or fully replacing one you've already Read. Overwriting an existing file you haven't Read will fail. For partial changes, use Edit instead.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to write (must be absolute, not relative)

content.description: The content to write to the file

tools.name: DeferredToolPlaceholder
tools.description: Reserved placeholder that keeps deferred tool loading active; never call this tool.

tools.name: mcp__codegraph__codegraph_explore
tools.description: PRIMARY TOOL — call FIRST for almost any question OR before an edit: how does X work, architecture, a bug, where/what is X, surveying an area, or the symbols you are about to change. Returns the verbatim source of the relevant symbols grouped by file in ONE capped call (Read-equivalent — treat the shown source as already Read; do NOT re-open those files), plus the call path among them. Query can be a natural-language question OR a bag of symbol/file names. Usually the ONLY call you need — more accurate context, in far fewer tokens and round-trips than a search/Read/Grep loop.

query.description: Symbol names, file names, or short code terms to explore (e.g., "AuthService loginUser session-manager", "GraphTraverser BFS impact traversal.ts"). For a flow question, name the symbols spanning the flow (e.g. "mutateElement renderScene"). A natural-language question works too — no prior codegraph_search needed.

maxFiles.description: Maximum number of files to include source code from (default: 12)

projectPath.description: Absolute path to the project to query (or any directory inside it) — codegraph uses the nearest .codegraph/ index at or above that path. Omit to use this session's default project. Pass it to query a second codebase, or when the server root has no index of its own (e.g. a monorepo where only sub-projects are indexed, so there is no default project).

content.text:
The following skills are available for use with the Skill tool:

- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs (plus reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups where the model's recipe covers them) at the effort level given first, before any target (low|medium|high|xhigh|max: from few high-confidence findings to many, some uncertain; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud (requires claude.ai account access)); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply them to the working tree after the review. Pass --max-findings <n> to report up to n findings, or --max-findings all for every finding. The choice stays until you pass --max-findings default. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option. - Use the max or ultra level only when the user, or instructions such as CLAUDE.md or a skill, explicitly ask for one, never on your own judgment: they are the costliest reviews and start many reviewer subagents.

- Use multiSelect: true to allow multiple answers to be selected for a question

tools.name: SendFeedback
tools.description:
Use this tool to draft feedback about Claude Code when you hit a high-signal moment. That includes both PRODUCT issues and MODEL-BEHAVIOR issues:
- a reproducible tool or product failure was just resolved or abandoned
- the user clearly expressed frustration with Claude Code or with how you handled the task
- you hit a missing capability that blocked a reasonable request
- you notice, or the user points out, that your own behavior in this session went wrong, for example: you gave a confident answer then had to retract it; you stopped short and handed work back when you could have finished; you declined or disputed a reasonable request; you spawned more subagents than the task warranted; your tone was off; you asked more clarifying questions than needed; you expanded scope beyond what was asked

The draft is QUEUED LOCALLY. It is never sent without the user's explicit approval, and calling this tool renders no UI and does not interrupt the conversation, so never announce it or ask the user about it mid-task.

Write `details` as short labeled bullets in this exact order, one to three lines each, no narrative paragraphs:
- **What happened:** the observed behavior vs. what was expected, with exact error text if short. Facts only.
- **What the user said:** the user's own words that prompted this, quoted. If nothing did, write "User didn't comment; observed by the model." Never paraphrase sentiment into a stronger claim.
- **Repro:** the minimal steps or shape that reproduces it.
- **Evidence:** identifiers a reader can chase, such as request IDs, timestamps, file paths, versions. Omit the bullet if there are none.

Constraints:
- Never fabricate or exaggerate user sentiment; report only what actually happened.
- Everything in the draft must be sourced from the user or the session, never inferred: leave unknown fields blank rather than guess, and add a final **Cause:** bullet only for a root cause you verified in-session.
- Use `area` to name the part of Claude Code the feedback is about (a feature, command, or workflow, e.g. "hooks config", "/help", "file editing") when there is a clear one; leave it blank otherwise.
- Use `failure_mode` ONLY when the report is about model behavior (how Claude responded), not a product bug. Pick the single closest value, or `other` when it is a model-behavior issue that fits no listed value; omit the field only when the report is a product/tool bug with no model-behavior component.
- Use `task_category` to name what kind of task the session was doing, or `other` when it is a clear task that fits no listed value. Omit only if genuinely unclear.
- Do not include secrets or credentials. Refer to people by role ("a teammate", "the PR reviewer"), never by name, email address, or chat/user ID. This applies inside quoted user words too: replace a name or handle with a bracketed role (e.g. "[a teammate]") and keep the rest verbatim. Do not include customer-facing channel or DM IDs, or excerpts of customer content. Session, request, and run IDs, timestamps, repo/PR numbers, and file paths (written relative to the working directory, or ~-prefixed, not absolute paths under the user's home) remain the right evidence.
- If the issue looks like a security vulnerability: describe the class of problem, never a working exploit or step-by-step extraction path.
- Draft only at the natural moments listed above, and at most one draft per distinct issue; never re-draft the same issue in a session.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

A workflow size guideline is configured for this session: small — keep workflows under 5 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale.

def _symbols(view: View, hint: str, limit: int) -> tuple[list[str], int]:
    """An exact name, or a dotted suffix of the declaration path (``Auth.refresh``).
    Returns the matches and the limit that cut them (0 when none did)."""
    parts = hint.split(".")
    named, truncated = view.named(parts[-1], NAMED_LIMIT)
    cut = NAMED_LIMIT if truncated else 0
    found = set()
    for key in named:
        if key.startswith("symbol:"):
            path = [segment.split("~")[0] for segment in key.rsplit("#", 1)[1].split(".")]
            if path[-len(parts) :] == parts:
                found.add(key)
        elif len(parts) == 1:
            found.add(key)
    if len(parts) > 1:
        modules, truncated = view.named(hint, NAMED_LIMIT)
        cut = NAMED_LIMIT if truncated else cut
        found.update(modules)
    ordered = sorted(found)
    if len(ordered) > limit:

`.rs` files report `FileInfo.language == "rust"`. These declarations become symbols:

| Rust declaration | Kind | Key segment |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `fn f`, a bodiless `fn f();` in an `extern` block | `function` | `f` |
| `struct S`, `enum E`, `union U` | `struct`, `enum`, `union` | `S` |
| `trait T` | `trait` | `T` |
| `fn m` or `fn m();` of a trait | `method`, nested in the trait | `T.m` |
| `impl Trait for Type`, `impl Type` | `impl` | `<impl Trait for Type>` |
| `fn m` of an impl | `method`, nested in the impl | `<impl Trait for Type>.m` |
| `const C` of an impl or trait | `constant`, nested | `<impl Type>.C` |
| `type A = ...;` | `type` | `A` |
| `const C`, `static S` | `constant`, `variable` | `C`, `S` |
| `macro_rules! m` | `macro` | `m` |

Keys are `symbol:<path>#<segment>`. Dotted symbol hints match this declaration path:
`new` or `<impl Store>.new`, not `Store.new` (an impl is a declaration, unlike Go's
receiver-named methods). An impl block is its own declaration site
(ADR-0010): its name is `<impl Trait for Type>` or `<impl Type>`, made of the trait
and self type as written (generic arguments kept, comments dropped, whitespace
squashed, `.` and `~` replaced by `_`, cut at 256 characters) and nothing else. The impl's
own generics (`impl<T: Clone>`) and `where` clause are not part of the name, so a comment
or a rewritten bound never changes identity. Equal sibling segments (several `impl Foo`
blocks, `cfg` variants of one function, an inline `mod` repeated) take `~n` in source
order; a method's ordinal belongs to its impl. `Entity.name` is the identifier
(`new`, not `Store.new`) or the impl's `<impl ...>` text; signatures are the declaration

scopes = facts.scopes
    # File-level spans by start. A tag definition nests in its declaration, so each span
    # knows its enclosing one and a byte's scope is the innermost span holding it.
    tops = sorted((d.start, d.end, k) for k, s in enumerate(scopes) if (d := s.decl))
    starts = [t[0] for t in tops]
    outer: list[int] = []
    stack: list[int] = []
    for start, _, _ in tops:
        while stack and start >= tops[stack[-1]][1]:
            stack.pop()
        outer.append(stack[-1] if stack else -1)
        stack.append(len(outer) - 1)

    def scope_at(at: int) -> int:
        j = bisect.bisect_right(starts, at) - 1
        while j >= 0 and at >= tops[j][1]:
            j = outer[j]
        return tops[j][2] if j >= 0 else 0

    # Declared names are not uses

scopes = facts.scopes
    # File-level spans by start. A tag definition nests in its declaration, so each span
    # knows its enclosing one and a byte's scope is the innermost span holding it.
    tops = sorted((d.start, d.end, k) for k, s in enumerate(scopes) if (d := s.decl))
    starts = [t[0] for t in tops]
    outer: list[int] = []
    stack: list[int] = []
    for start, _, _ in tops:
        while stack and start >= tops[stack[-1]][1]:
            stack.pop()
        outer.append(stack[-1] if stack else -1)
        stack.append(len(outer) - 1)

    def scope_at(at: int) -> int:
        j = bisect.bisect_right(starts, at) - 1
        while j >= 0 and at >= tops[j][1]:
            j = outer[j]
        return tops[j][2] if j >= 0 else 0

    # Declared names are not uses

only walks the declaration containers and assigns each use to the innermost symbol
whose span holds it. A name bound anywhere in a symbol (parameters, locals, template
parameters, fields of a class) is opaque in all of it: no block scoping, no types.

from dataclasses import dataclass, field

TAGS = {
    "class_specifier": "class",
    "struct_specifier": "struct",
    "union_specifier": "union",
    "enum_specifier": "enum",
}

    (call_expression function: [(identifier) (qualified_identifier) (template_function)

    (type_identifier) @type
    (qualified_identifier) @qualified
    (base_class_clause [(type_identifier) (qualified_identifier) (template_type)] @base)
    [(class_specifier name: (_) body: (_)) (struct_specifier name: (_) body: (_))
      (union_specifier name: (_) body: (_)) (enum_specifier name: (_) body: (_))] @local
    (parameter_declaration declarator: (_) @bind)
    (optional_parameter_declaration declarator: (_) @bind)
    (variadic_parameter_declaration declarator: (_) @bind)
    (declaration declarator: (_) @bind)
    (field_declaration declarator: (_) @bind)

    (structured_binding_declarator (identifier) @bind)
    (type_parameter_declaration (type_identifier) @bind)

"""C++ language slice: tree-sitter syntax facts (docs/cpp.md); resolution is in ``cpp_resolve``.

Symbols are namespace blocks, classes, structs, unions and enums with a body, functions
and methods (definitions, prototypes and out-of-line definitions such as
``int Box::get()``), typedefs and aliases, namespace-scope variables and macros, nested
as written. The preprocessor never runs. One compiled query collects every use; Python
only walks the declaration containers and assigns each use to the innermost symbol
whose span holds it. A name bound anywhere in a symbol (parameters, locals, template
parameters, a class's fields) is opaque in all of it: no block scoping, no types.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import re
from collections.abc import Iterator
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Any

import tree_sitter_cpp
from tree_sitter import Language, Node, Parser, Query, QueryCursor

from oxide.core.languages.c import _KEYWORDS as C_KEYWORDS
from oxide.core.languages.c import _LEXEMES, _WRAPPERS, Include, _blank, _line, innermost
from oxide.core.languages.java import Call
from oxide.core.languages.python import TOO_DEEP, Use, as_list, syntax_diagnostics, too_deep

VERSION = "oxide-cpp-v1"
# The JSON shape of ``Parsed`` that generations retain for reuse; bump on any change.
FACTS_VERSION = "oxide-cpp-facts-v1"
CLASSES = ("class", "struct", "union")
KINDS = ("namespace", *CLASSES, "enum", "function", "type", "variable", "macro")
TAGS = {
    "class_specifier": "class",
    "struct_specifier": "struct",
    "union_specifier": "union",
    "enum_specifier": "enum",
}

LANGUAGE = Language(tree_sitter_cpp.language())
_QUERY = Query(
    LANGUAGE,
    """
    (preproc_include path: [(string_literal) (system_lib_string)] @include)
    (call_expression function: [(identifier) (qualified_identifier) (template_function)
      (field_expression argument: (this))] @call arguments: (argument_list) @arguments)
    (type_identifier) @type
    (qualified_identifier) @qualified
    (base_class_clause [(type_identifier) (qualified_identifier) (template_type)] @base)
    [(class_specifier name: (_) body: (_)) (struct_specifier name: (_) body: (_))
      (union_specifier name: (_) body: (_)) (enum_specifier name: (_) body: (_))] @local
    (parameter_declaration declarator: (_) @bind)
    (optional_parameter_declaration declarator: (_) @bind)
    (variadic_parameter_declaration declarator: (_) @bind)
    (declaration declarator: (_) @bind)
    (field_declaration declarator: (_) @bind)
    (type_definition declarator: (_) @bind)
    (for_range_loop declarator: (_) @bind)
    (structured_binding_declarator (identifier) @bind)
    (type_parameter_declaration (type_identifier) @bind)
    (optional_type_parameter_declaration name: (_) @bind)
    (variadic_type_parameter_declaration (type_identifier) @bind)
    (alias_declaration name: (_) @bind)
    (using_declaration) @using
    """,
)
_BROKEN = Query(LANGUAGE, "(ERROR) @error (MISSING) @missing")
# ``class API Name : Base {``: an export macro between the key and the name breaks the
# grammar, so the parser sees an all-caps word there as spaces (offsets kept).
_EXPORT = re.compile(
    rb"\b(?:class|struct|union)\s+([A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*)\s+(?=[A-Za-z_]\w*\s*(?:final\s*)?"
    rb"(?:\{|:(?!:)\s*[A-Za-z_]))"
)
# A ``.h`` file is C++ when, outside comments and literals, it has C++-only syntax.
_CPLUSPLUS = re.compile(
    rb"\b(?:namespace\s+\w*\s*\{|template\s*<|class\s+\w+\s*(?:final\s*)?[:{]"
    rb"|(?:public|private|protected)\s*:(?!:))|\w::~?\w"
)
_NAMES = (
    "identifier",
    "field_identifier",
    "type_identifier",
    "qualified_identifier",
    "destructor_name",
    "operator_name",
    "operator_cast",
    "template_function",
)
_INNER = ("parenthesized_declarator", "reference_declarator", "variadic_declarator")
_CONDITIONAL = ("preproc_if", "preproc_ifdef", "preproc_else", "preproc_elif", "preproc_elifdef")
_KEYWORDS = C_KEYWORDS | frozenset(
    b"alignas alignof catch class concept consteval constexpr constinit co_await co_return"
    b" co_yield decltype delete explicit export false final friend mutable namespace new"
    b" noexcept nullptr operator override private protected public requires static_assert"
    b" template this thread_local throw true try typeid typename using virtual".split()
)


def is_cplusplus(data: bytes) -> bool:
    """Whether a ``.h`` file is C++ (docs/cpp.md); C otherwise."""
    return _CPLUSPLUS.search(_LEXEMES.sub(b" ", data)) is not None


@dataclass(slots=True)
class Decl:
    kind: str
    name: str
    qualifier: str  # ``A::B`` of ``int A::B::f()``; a leading ``::`` is absolute
    start: int
    end: int
    signature: str
    static: bool  # internal linkage: visible only where its file is
    defines: bool  # a function with a body (a prototype otherwise)
    low: int  # a function's fewest and most arguments (-1: variadic); 0 otherwise
    high: int


@dataclass(slots=True)
class Scope:
    parent: int
    decl: Decl | None
    bound: set[str] = field(default_factory=set)
    usings: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)  # ``using namespace`` targets
    bases: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)  # a class's base classes, as written
    calls: list[Call] = field(default_factory=list)
    refs: list[Use] = field(default_factory=list)  # type names, qualified or not


@dataclass(slots=True)
class Parsed:
    """Scope 0 is the file: code outside any symbol."""

    includes: list[Include]
    scopes: list[Scope]
    diagnostics: list[str]


def _text(data: bytes, node: Node | None) -> str:
    return "" if node is None else data[node.start_byte : node.end_byte].decode("utf-8", "replace")


def _squash(text: str | bytes) -> str:
    return " ".join((text if isinstance(text, str) else text.decode("utf-8", "replace")).split())


def qualified(data: bytes, node: Node | None) -> list[str] | None:
    """The parts of a (qualified) name, ``""`` first for a leading ``::``; template
    arguments dropped. None for a keyword or anything else."""
    parts: list[str] = []
    while node is not None and node.type == "qualified_identifier":
        scope = node.child_by_field_name("scope")
        if scope is not None and scope.type == "template_type":
            scope = scope.child_by_field_name("name")
        if scope is not None and scope.type not in ("namespace_identifier", "type_identifier"):
            return None
        parts.append(_text(data, scope))
        node = node.child_by_field_name("name")
    if node is not None and node.type in ("template_function", "template_type", "template_method"):
        node = node.child_by_field_name("name")
    if node is None:
        return None
    if node.type == "destructor_name":
        last = "~" + _text(data, node.named_children[-1] if node.named_children else None)
    elif node.type == "operator_name":
        last = _squash(_text(data, node))
    elif node.type == "operator_cast":
        last = "operator " + _squash(_text(data, node.child_by_field_name("type")))
    elif node.type in _NAMES or node.type == "namespace_identifier":
        last = _text(data, node)
    else:
        return None
    if last.encode() in _KEYWORDS or not last.strip("~") or any(p in _KEYWORDS_STR for p in parts):
        return None
    return [*parts, last]


_KEYWORDS_STR = frozenset(k.decode() for k in _KEYWORDS)


def _declared(node: Node | None) -> tuple[Node | None, Node | None]:
    """The name a declarator declares and its function declarator, if it declares a
    function (not a pointer to one): the innermost wrapper decides."""
    function: Node | None = None
    while node is not None and node.type not in _NAMES:
        if node.type in _INNER:
            node = node.named_children[-1] if node.named_children else None
            continue
        if node.type not in _WRAPPERS:
            return None, None
        function = node if node.type == "function_declarator" else None
        inner = node.child_by_field_name("declarator")
        # ``API T name(...)``: recovery takes ``T`` as the name and keeps ``name`` in an
        # ERROR before the parameters.
        broken = [c for c in node.children if c.type == "ERROR"] if function else []
        if broken and broken[0].named_children:
            last = broken[0].named_children[-1]
            inner = last if last.type == "identifier" else inner
        if inner is None and node.type == "attributed_declarator" and node.named_children:
            inner = node.named_children[0]
        node = inner
    if node is not None and node.type == "operator_cast":
        function = node  # ``operator bool() const`` holds its own parameters
    if node is not None and node.type == "qualified_identifier":
        last = node
        while (name := last.child_by_field_name("name")) is not None and name.type == "qualified_identifier":
            last = name
        if name is not None and name.type == "operator_cast":
            function = name
    return node, function


def _arity(function: Node) -> tuple[int, int]:
    """Fewest and most arguments a function declarator takes (-1: any number)."""
    params = function.child_by_field_name("parameters")
    if params is None:  # a conversion function: ``operator T() const``
        abstract = function.child_by_field_name("declarator")
        params = abstract.child_by_field_name("parameters") if abstract is not None else None
    low = high = 0
    for p in params.children if params is not None else []:
        if p.type in ("...", "variadic_parameter_declaration"):
            return low, -1
        if p.type == "optional_parameter_declaration":
            high += 1
        elif p.type == "parameter_declaration" and p.text != b"void":
            low, high = low + 1, high + 1
    return low, high


def _static(node: Node) -> bool:
    return any(c.type == "storage_class_specifier" and c.text == b"static" for c in node.children)


type Frame = tuple[Iterator[Node], int, bool]  # children, parent scope, internal linkage


class _Facts:
    def __init__(self, data: bytes) -> None:
        self.data = data
        self.scopes = [Scope(0, None)]
        self.names: set[int] = set()  # start bytes of declared symbol names

    def add(self, parent: int, kind: str, parts: list[str], name: Node, span: Node, *rest: Any) -> int:
        qualifier = "::".join(parts[:-1]) if parts[:-1] != [""] else "::"
        if parts[:1] == [""] and len(parts) > 2:
            qualifier = "::" + qualifier[2:] if qualifier.startswith("::") else "::" + qualifier
        decl = Decl(kind, parts[-1], qualifier, span.start_byte, span.end_byte, *rest)
        self.scopes.append(Scope(parent, decl))
        self.names.add(name.start_byte)
        return len(self.scopes) - 1

    def signature(self, span: Node, cut: Node | None, end: int | None = None) -> str:
        """``span``'s text without ``cut`` (a body), whitespace collapsed."""
        data, stop = self.data, end if end is not None else span.end_byte
        if cut is None:
            return _squash(data[span.start_byte : stop])
        return _squash(data[span.start_byte : cut.start_byte] + data[cut.end_byte : stop])

    def walk(self, root: Node) -> None:
        stack: list[Frame] = [(iter(root.children), 0, False)]
        while stack:
            children, parent, static = stack[-1]
            node = next(children, None)
            if node is None:
                stack.pop()
            elif (frame := self.declaration(node, node, parent, static)) is not None:
                stack.append(frame)

    def member(self, parent: int) -> bool:
        decl = self.scopes[parent].decl
        return decl is not None and decl.kind in CLASSES

    def declaration(self, node: Node, span: Node, parent: int, static: bool) -> Frame | None:
        """Adds the symbols ``node`` declares; the frame of its members, if any."""
        kind, data = node.type, self.data
        if kind in _CONDITIONAL or kind == "ERROR":
            return iter(node.children), parent, static
        if kind == "linkage_specification":
            body = node.child_by_field_name("body")
            if body is not None and body.type == "declaration_list":
                return iter(body.children), parent, static
            return self.declaration(body, body, parent, static) if body is not None else None
        if kind == "template_declaration":
            skip = ("template_parameter_list", "requires_clause")
            inner = [c for c in node.named_children if c.type not in skip]
            return self.declaration(inner[-1], span, parent, static) if inner else None
        if kind == "namespace_definition":
            return self.namespace(node, parent, static)
        if kind in TAGS:
            return self.tag(node, span, parent, static)
        if kind in ("preproc_def", "preproc_function_def"):
            name = node.child_by_field_name("name")
            if name is not None:
                shown = _line(_text(data, node)).removesuffix("\\").rstrip()
                self.add(parent, "macro", [_text(data, name)], name, node, shown, False, False, 0, 0)
        elif kind == "function_definition":
            name, function = _declared(node.child_by_field_name("declarator"))
            parts = qualified(data, name)
            if parts is None or name is None or function is None:
                return None
            body = node.child_by_field_name("body")
            ends = ("field_initializer_list", "compound_statement", "try_statement")
            cut = next((c.start_byte for c in node.children if c.type in ends), None)
            internal = static or (_static(node) and not self.member(parent))
            shown = self.signature(span, None, cut)
            self.add(parent, "function", parts, name, span, shown, internal, body is not None, *_arity(function))
        elif kind == "alias_declaration":
            name = node.child_by_field_name("name")
            if name is not None:
                shown = self.signature(span, None)
                self.add(parent, "type", [_text(data, name)], name, span, shown, static, False, 0, 0)
        elif kind in ("declaration", "field_declaration", "type_definition"):
            return self.declarators(node, span, parent, static)
        return None

    def declarators(self, node: Node, span: Node, parent: int, static: bool) -> Frame | None:
        """A declaration's tag definition, then each declarator; the tag's frame."""
        member = self.member(parent)
        internal = static or (_static(node) and not member)
        tag = node.child_by_field_name("type")
        frame = self.tag(tag, None, parent, internal)
        typedef = node.type == "type_definition"
        body = tag.child_by_field_name("body") if frame is not None and tag is not None else None
        signature = self.signature(span, body)
        for declarator in node.children_by_field_name("declarator"):
            name, function = _declared(declarator)
            parts = qualified(self.data, name)
            if parts is None or name is None or (name.type == "type_identifier") != typedef:
                continue
            if typedef:
                self.add(parent, "type", parts, name, span, signature, internal, False, 0, 0)
            elif function is not None:
                arity = _arity(function)
                self.add(parent, "function", parts, name, span, signature, internal, False, *arity)
            elif not member:  # fields are not symbols; they are bound in their class
                shown = _line(signature)
                self.add(parent, "variable", parts, name, span, shown, internal, False, 0, 0)
        return frame

    def namespace(self, node: Node, parent: int, static: bool) -> Frame | None:
        name, body = node.child_by_field_name("name"), node.child_by_field_name("body")
        if body is None:
            return None
        if name is None:  # anonymous: its members have internal linkage
            return iter(body.children), parent, True
        named = name.named_children if name.type == "nested_namespace_specifier" else [name]
        parts = [_text(self.data, c) for c in named]
        if not parts or any(not p or p in _KEYWORDS_STR for p in parts):
            return iter(body.children), parent, static
        shown = f"namespace {'::'.join(parts)}"
        k = self.add(parent, "namespace", parts, name, node, shown, static, False, 0, 0)
        return iter(body.children), k, static

    def tag(self, node: Node | None, span: Node | None, parent: int, static: bool) -> Frame | None:
        """A class, struct, union or enum with a body as a symbol; its members' frame."""
        if node is None or node.type not in TAGS:
            return None
        name, body = node.child_by_field_name("name"), node.child_by_field_name("body")
        parts = qualified(self.data, name)
        if name is None or body is None or parts is None:
            return None
        span = span or node
        shown = self.signature(span, body, node.end_byte)
        k = self.add(parent, TAGS[node.type], parts, name, span, shown, static, False, 0, 0)
        return (iter(body.children), k, static) if node.type != "enum_specifier" else None


def _hidden(match: re.Match[bytes]) -> bytes:
    start, end = match.span(1)
    text = match.group()
    return text[: start - match.start()] + b" " * (end - start) + text[end - match.start() :]


def parse(data: bytes) -> Parsed | str:
    """Syntax facts, or the reason the file is unsupported."""
    try:
        data.decode("utf-8")
    except UnicodeDecodeError:
        return "C++ source is not UTF-8"
    seen = _LEXEMES.sub(_blank, data) if b"/*" in data else data
    root = Parser(LANGUAGE).parse(_EXPORT.sub(_hidden, seen)).root_node
    if too_deep(root):
        return TOO_DEEP
    captures = QueryCursor(_QUERY).captures(root)
    facts = _Facts(data)
    facts.walk(root)
    scopes = facts.scopes
    scope_at = innermost([(d.start, d.end, k) for k, s in enumerate(scopes) if (d := s.decl)])
    _uses(data, captures, facts.names, scopes, scope_at)
    includes = []
    for node in captures.get("include", []):
        text = _text(data, node)
        if len(text) > 2:
            includes.append(Include(text[1:-1], node.type == "system_lib_string", node.start_byte, node.end_byte))
    includes.sort(key=lambda item: (item.start, item.end))
    for scope in scopes:
        scope.calls.sort(key=lambda u: (u.start, u.end))
        scope.refs.sort(key=lambda u: (u.start, u.end))
    return Parsed(includes, scopes, syntax_diagnostics(root, _BROKEN))


def _uses(
    data: bytes, captures: dict[str, list[Node]], names: set[int], scopes: list[Scope], scope_at: Any
) -> None:
    """Assigns bindings, ``using`` directives, bases, calls and type uses to scopes."""
    skip = set(names)  # declared names are not uses
    for node in captures.get("local", []):
        name = node.child_by_field_name("name")
        if name is not None and name.start_byte not in names:
            skip.add(name.start_byte)
            if (parts := qualified(data, name)) is not None:
                scopes[scope_at(node.start_byte)].bound.add(parts[-1])
    for node in captures.get("bind", []):
        name, _ = _declared(node)
        if name is not None and (parts := qualified(data, name)) is not None:
            skip.add(name.start_byte)
            if name.start_byte not in names and len(parts) == 1:
                scopes[scope_at(name.start_byte)].bound.add(parts[0])
    for node in captures.get("using", []):
        target = node.named_children[-1] if node.named_children else None
        parts = qualified(data, target)
        if parts is not None:
            scope = scopes[scope_at(node.start_byte)]
            if any(c.type == "namespace" for c in node.children):
                scope.usings.append("::".join(parts))
            else:  # ``using X::n``: ``n`` is opaque where it is brought in
                scope.bound.add(parts[-1])
    taken: set[tuple[int, int]] = set()  # qualified names already read as part of another
    for node, arguments in zip(captures.get("call", []), captures.get("arguments", []), strict=True):
        taken.add((node.start_byte, node.end_byte))
        if node.type == "field_expression":
            parts = qualified(data, node.child_by_field_name("field"))
            name = f"this->{parts[-1]}" if parts and len(parts) == 1 else None
        else:
            parts = qualified(data, node)
            name = "::".join(parts) if parts and parts[-1][0] not in "~o" or parts and parts[-1].isidentifier() else None
        if name is not None:
            arity = sum(1 for c in arguments.named_children if c.type != "comment")
            call = Call(name, node.start_byte, node.end_byte, arity)
            scopes[scope_at(node.start_byte)].calls.append(call)
    for node in captures.get("qualified", []):
        inner = node.child_by_field_name("name")
        if inner is not None and inner.type == "qualified_identifier":
            taken.add((inner.start_byte, inner.end_byte))
    for node in captures.get("qualified", []):
        if (node.start_byte, node.end_byte) in taken:
            continue
        last = node
        while (inner := last.child_by_field_name("name")) is not None and inner.type == "qualified_identifier":
            last = inner
        if inner is None or inner.type not in ("type_identifier", "template_type"):
            continue
        skip.add(inner.start_byte)
        if (parts := qualified(data, node)) is not None and node.start_byte not in names:
            scopes[scope_at(node.start_byte)].refs.append(Use("::".join(parts), node.start_byte, node.end_byte))
    for node in captures.get("base", []):
        parts = qualified(data, node)
        if parts is not None:
            scopes[scope_at(node.start_byte)].bases.append("::".join(parts))
    for node in captures.get("type", []):
        if node.start_byte not in skip:
            scopes[scope_at(node.start_byte)].refs.append(Use(_text(data, node), node.start_byte, node.end_byte))
